walkthroughs.body_html:
International Trade and the Global Economy — a core area of GCSE Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

International Trade and the Global Economy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with International Trade and the Global Economy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Specialisation based on lowest opportunity cost is:
options: Absolute advantage
Comparative advantage
Free trade
Protectionism

mcqs.q: A tariff is a tax on:
options: Exports
Imports
Domestic production
Consumption

mcqs.q: What does Income Elasticity of Demand (YED) tell us?
options: YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
A negative YED means the demand calculation went wrong.
The sign tells us the good type: positive YED = normal good (rises with income); negative YED = inferior good (falls with income). YED > 1 indicates a luxury; YED between 0 and 1 a necessity.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.

mcqs.q: What is asymmetric information as a source of market failure?
options: Asymmetric information means a buyer and seller disagree about a price.

When one party in a transaction knows more than the other — leading to problems like adverse selection (used-car market) or moral hazard (insurance). Markets can fail or unravel when information is unequal.
Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.

mcqs.q: Why do economists generally argue against protectionism?
options: Tariffs and quotas raise prices for consumers, protect inefficient industries, invite retaliation, and reduce overall welfare — even when they save specific jobs, the cost per job saved typically exceeds the wage.
Protectionism always makes a country richer by keeping money at home.
Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
